identification.summary: CardinalLizard is a Kaspersky-named, China-linked (Chinese-speaking) threat actor described by Kaspersky in its Q1 2018 APT trends reporting as increasing its interest in Malaysia while keeping an existing focus on the Philippines, Russia and Mongolia [S1][S2]. Malpedia summarizes it as a China-linked actor targeting Asian entities since 2018, using spear-phishing, custom malware with anti-detection features and possibly infrastructure shared with other actors [S3].
identification.firstObserved: Malpedia: active since 2018 [S3]. Kaspersky Q1 2018 reporting already discusses the cluster, so public naming is no later than 2018-04 [S1].
identification.notes: Name originates with Kaspersky (GReAT); Malpedia credits the 2018-12-05 'APT review of the year' (Costin Raiu, Vicente Diaz) for the entry [S3]. Kaspersky's Q1 2018 reporting describes ShaggyPanther as a distinct cluster (government targets in Taiwan and Malaysia); one search summary suggested it may be an alias in the 2018 review, which is unverified, so it is not merged here [S1]. CardinalRAT (Unit 42, 2017) is an unrelated malware family and is not linked to this actor in any source seen.

attribution.confidence: Kaspersky characterizes the activity as Chinese-speaking; no source seen attributes CardinalLizard to a specific PRC agency or contractor [S1][S3].
attribution.basis: Language/regional-targeting based vendor clustering by Kaspersky [S1]; secondary catalog entry [S3]. Underlying technical evidence not reviewed.

targeting.notes: Regional focus from Kaspersky Q1 2018 highlights as relayed in search summaries; victim sectors not found in sources seen [S1][S2].

capabilities.summary: Malpedia states the actor uses spear-phishing, custom malware with anti-detection features and possibly shared infrastructure with other actors [S3]. A third-party catalog reports no CVEs attributed to the actor and Malpedia lists no associated malware families [S3][S4].
